prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK “Contract” 2024 (policies and costings only)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration and stop small-boat crossings.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero policies/levies and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Key policies by area
- Immigration: Freeze non-essential visas; create a Department of Immigration; detain and deport illegal arrivals (including offshore processing); bar asylum from safe-country entrants; deport foreign criminals post-sentence; restrict student dependants; 5-year residency/employment requirement for benefits; employer immigration tax (NI 20% on foreign workers, exemptions for essential health/care and very small firms). Claimed savings £5–10bn pa; employer tax revenue £4bn pa.

- Government spending/waste: End interest on QE reserves (~£35bn pa saving); 5% efficiency saving across departments (£50bn pa); cut foreign aid by 50% (£6bn pa); deregulation “Brexit bonus”; improve HMRC collection. Claimed total potential savings £91bn pa.

- Personal taxation/cost of living: Raise income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000; cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies; cut Stamp Duty (0% below £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% >£1.5m); restore VAT-free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m (20% above). Cost £70bn pa.

- Business: Lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; reduce main CT to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high-street SMEs (offset by 4% online delivery tax); planning reform; deregulation; tax simplification. Cost £18bn pa.

- NHS: Zero basic-rate tax for NHS/social care frontline for 3 years; lift training caps; fee write-offs tied to service; use independent capacity (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks; efficiency measures; “Pharmacy First” push; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms. Cost £17bn pa.

- Energy/Net Zero: Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies; tax renewables to offset subsidy removal; fast-track North Sea and shale test sites; expand SMRs and other technologies. Claimed savings £30bn pa.

- Policing: +40,000 officers over 5 years; expand stop and search; mandatory sentences for violent/knife offences and drug trafficking; leadership/recruitment changes; reduce DE&I roles. Cost £3bn pa.

- Justice: Mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; increase budget from £10bn to £12bn; change hate-crime definition; build 10,000 detention places; measures on grooming gangs and youth crime. Cost £2bn pa.

- Education: Curriculum changes; restrict gender-transition practices in schools; 20% tax relief on independent schools; scrap interest on student loans, extend repayment to 45 years; limit undergraduate numbers with minimum entry standards; expand PRUs; 2‑year degree option. Cost £5bn pa.

- Benefits: Tighter conditionality (2-strike job offer rule; face-to-face assessments); incentives and training to move up to 2m into work. Claimed savings £15bn pa.

- Brexit: Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; distance from EU defence initiatives; prepare to renegotiate the Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

- Defence: Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% within 6 years; pay review; service-justice bill; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform; education support. Cost £14bn pa.

- Housing: Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; scrap Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leaseholder protections; construction tech. Neutral cost.

- Children/families: Targeted marriage tax allowance when affordable (25% transferable); front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single‑sex spaces; inquiry into social media harms; review Online Safety Bill. Cost £8bn pa.

- Transport/infrastructure: Scrap HS2 remainder (one‑off £25bn saving); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; no ICE car bans; regional road/rail upgrades; new 50/50 public–pension‑fund ownership model for utilities; merge infrastructure bodies. Savings: £25bn one‑off; £5bn pa.

- Agriculture: Raise budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies with direct payments; support small farms; country sports protections; anti–price‑fixing powers; “Buy British” targets; cut red tape. Cost £2bn pa.

- Fishing/coasts: Restrict foreign access and supertrawlers; licence fees; expand patrols; rebuild processing; fleet incentives; sustainable stock management. Cost £2bn pa.

- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; curb offshore tax avoidance in care; pension system review; implement Mineworkers Pension Scheme reform recommendations.

- Constitutional reform: Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform Lords and civil service leadership; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights. Neutral cost.

- “Reclaiming Britain”: Sovereignty positions (WHO/WEF/CBDC); replace Equality Act; Free Speech Bill; scrap BBC licence fee; new public holidays; anti‑corruption unit. Neutral cost.

Funding summary
- Claimed savings: £150bn pa plus £10bn pa from growth assumptions = £160bn pa.
- Total annual costs of pledges: £141bn pa.
